name: Slav Defense
blurb: Black defends d5 with ...c6 instead of ...e6, so the c8 bishop stays free. Very solid against 1.d4 and 2.c4.

lines.name: Czech Variation, Classical System, Main Line
Czech Variation, Carlsbad Variation, Morozevich Variation

ideas.d4 d5: Claims the centre and stops White from playing e4 for free.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 c6: Supports d5 with a pawn and, unlike ...e6, keeps the c8 bishop's diagonal open.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6: Develops and adds a second defender to d5.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4: Takes the c4 pawn, ready to hold it with ...b5 if White is careless.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5: With ...b5 ruled out by a4, Black develops the bishop outside the pawn chain before playing ...e6.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e: Now that the bishop is out, ...e6 frees the f8 bishop without shutting anything in.
Pins the c3 knight to White's king.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 e4 b5: Holds on to the extra pawn on c4.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5 cxd5: Against the Exchange, recapturing with the pawn keeps a pawn in the centre and the position level.
ideas.d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bf5: White's e3 has shut in the c1 bishop, so Black develops the c8 bishop first, outside the pawn chain.
